chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The remarriage (raj'ah) is in sexual intercourse; otherwise, it is only one revocation. We have fully detailed in the conditions of the revocable divorce (talaq al-'iddah) what relates to that in our Great Book, and something of it has preceded.

key_terms.الْجِمَاعُ: Jima': Sexual intercourse, cited here as the condition establishing the revocation.
key_terms.الْمُرَاجَعَةُ: Raj'ah: The act of a husband taking back his divorced wife during the waiting period without a new contract.
key_terms.شَرَائِطُ: Sharā'it: Conditions or requirements for a legal ruling.
key_terms.طَلَاقُ الْعِدَّةِ: Talaq al-'iddah: Revocable divorce, where the wife remains in the waiting period and can be taken back.

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a valid revocable divorce (raj'ah) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar establishes that sexual intercourse (jima') is the definitive legal act that consummates the revocable divorce (talaq al-raj'i), allowing the husband to reclaim his wife without a new contract. The phrasing 'only one' suggests that a single act suffices to validate the raj'ah, distinguishing it from the finality of the third divorce. This ruling is central to Shia fiqh regarding the interim period (iddah) and is elaborated upon in al-Tusi's magnum opus, al-Kabir.
